NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>SOURCE 1–2 establish the same elongated building through its zigzag ramp end, projecting two-level glazed perimeter and curved roof. SOURCE 3 shows recessed lower glazing and exposed columns beneath projecting walkways; SOURCE 4 shows the timber roof underside, open interior and spiral stair. SOURCE 5–8 provide sections, plans and assembly diagrams showing the retained frame, added roof storey and outer buffer zone. CURRENT contains these broad exterior systems, but its roof-to-enclosure proportions differ visibly. The ramp-end view also shows unresolved landing connections. Repeated uncut obliques do not verify the source interior, floor voids or stair arrangement. No confirmed dimensions are supplied; screenshots cannot establish actual joint connectivity or hidden geometry.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="roof">problem: In SOURCE 1–2, the roof’s lowest central edge remains appreciably above the horizontal outer enclosure top, leaving a visible band of upper-storey glazing. In CURRENT 15, that central edge nearly meets the enclosure top, compressing this defining glazed band. The unequal high ends also appear reversed relative to SOURCE 1; camera handedness remains uncertain.
action: Locally adjust the roof profile and corresponding upper glazing/support heights to restore the source-backed central clearance. Establish matching ramp-end orientation before assigning the higher roof edge; retain the existing lower building during this correction.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="left">problem: CURRENT 15 shows the upper diagonal ramp/rail assembly extending beyond the right enclosure edge without a clearly resolved landing connection. SOURCE 1–2 show ramp flights terminating at identifiable perimeter landings. Dense overlapping lines in CURRENT obscure whether these are connected joints or passing intersections.
action: Review the ramp-end landing closeups against the source, then locally trim or connect only confirmed overshooting ramp and rail ends. Verify deck-to-landing contact and continuous guarding; do not treat projected overlap as a completed joint.</issue>
<keep>The straight horizontal top edge of the outer glazed enclosure, separate from the curved roof.
The existing roof’s smooth concave curvature; retain that character while correcting its vertical profile.</keep>
